restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) in the memory-efficient framework of [LLWS26], with the paper's 38-step characteristic and the Step-1 solution S read off its published SFS pair (member x = the message printed second). Step 2 accepts a first block iff s0(W7+d7)-s0(W7) = t7 (the exact requirement; p2 = 2^-3.90197); Step 3 tries the 1 element(s) of the exact set L* and checks every cell of rows 16..37 with early abort (proof.md Section 4).

Cost: fixed caps N_G = 5,112,833,347,910,986,158,445 groups of 2^29 batches (N = 2^103.92197 first blocks, 7 per counted 7x36-bit SWAR batch of 1525 operations) and V_MAX = 182,789,275,323,689,412,266,440,273,215,593 operations for all data-dependent work (halt on overflow). The exact total, including the generous allowances A_S = 2^74 (Step-1 SAT solve), A_C = 2^78 (characteristic search), DEV = 2^64 (all development) and the preprocessing, is 2^100.337240 target compressions on every run (cert.py, proof.md Section 8); claimed rounded up as 100.33724.

Success probability at least 0.3934 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks) and H2 (Step-3 probability q3 >= 2^-101.02, the one-sided 99% lower bound of a preregistered 32-seed sequential Monte-Carlo estimate, rounded down, corroborated by an organizer-run replica; disjointness factor 1). No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory (a reported metric): 2^95 bytes claimed, an unconditional word-RAM bound covering every charged computation, not only the online attack. A computation of K primitives stores at most K words; the preprocessing (A_C + A_S + DEV + pre/C = 2^78.08755 units, at most 2^89.50 primitives) therefore uses at most 2^94.50 bytes at 32 bytes per word, and the online attack holds below 2^16 bytes. For information, the largest process we ran used 31 GB RSS (the aborted SMC v1 freeze, proof.md Section 6.3). baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: For the attack's first blocks (per group W0..W14 from two uniform random 256-bit words; lane l of batch k uses W15 = 2^29 l + k), the chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) of distinct trials behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: (a) a trial is valid (s0(W7+d7)-s0(W7) = t7) with probability exactly p2 = 2^-3.90197; (b) conditioned on validity, W0..W5 are uniform, (W6, W7) is uniform on the Step-2 sets, and hence W16..W21 are iid uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemmas 1-2); (c) trials, and batches, are independent (success bound and the Hoeffding bound on the work cap).
heuristics.scope: Step 2 (p2), the distribution of the second-block words used to define q3 (Step 3), the trial cap N and the work cap V_MAX. Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the attack's own grouped family with full 38-step compressions (grouprate.c, 939,524,096 trials): W7 passes 62852548 against 62849024 expected, valid lanes 62852548 against 62849024 (rate 2^-3.90189, exact 2^-3.90197), batches with >= 1 valid lane 51555258 against 51552089, with >= 2 valid lanes 10068288 against 10067868; every deviation within 1.3 standard deviations. The extraction harness measured the paper's Step-2 conditions at 2^-4.0001 on 2^30 random first blocks through real compressions. The organizer experiment d1-first-block-r38 runs the shipped program on organizer seeds; about 196.2 of 256 returned pairs are expected under H1, and the count is a witness observation only, not a statistical test (no independence of the organizer's trials is assumed); our local run on 256 own seeds returned 188, and a local emulation of the organizer's public-seed request (the only run on organizer seeds, after the fix-1 design freeze) returned 198.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem. The tests cover about 2^30 first blocks, not 2^103.9, and cannot see a full-scale deviation. Only W15 varies inside a group (23 steps follow it). The organizer experiment's observations are participant numbers; its returned-pair count is the organizer-visible statistic. Run selection: none; every run is listed in proof.md Section 12.

heuristics.statement: (a) For a valid first block, q3 = the average over l in L* of Pr[the pair of l follows every cell of rows 16..37 and the paper's printed two-bit conditions on those rows (with the corrected reading W25[4] = W25[6])] is at least q3_model = 2^-101.02; this q3 is at most the algorithm's per-l success probability. (b) |L*| = 1, so no disjointness factor is needed (kappa = 1). (c) The preregistered sample is complete: every seed run under the frozen parameters is in it (the aborted first freeze and all development seeds are reported separately in proof.md Section 12).
heuristics.scope: The per-trial success probability p_model = p2 |L*| q3_model kappa = 2^-104.92197, hence the trial cap N (N p_model >= 1/2) and the success bound 0.3934.
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the second-block words have an exactly known distribution, so q3 is a fixed number and the sequential Monte-Carlo estimator of smc.py (exact enumeration of row 16, exact importance weights for the fresh rows, deterministic tail) is unbiased for it. Preregistered (program hashes, parameters, 32 seeds, rule frozen before any listed seed ran): mean 2^-100.9941, relative sd 0.029, one-sided 99% Student lower bound 2^-101.0121, q3_model = 2^-101.02. Stage factors are within 0.01 of integers. Row 16 agrees with a direct measurement on 2^35 uniform chaining values; the total is compared with the paper's condition count (102) in proof.md Section 6.4. Organizer-executed: experiment d1-q3-smc-r38 runs a standard-library replica of the estimator (exact row 16, 20 reduced replicates on organizer seeds, every success rebuilt and verified as a 38-step semi-free-start collision) with a pass rule frozen before any validation run (the mean of the 20 estimates >= 2^-101.40); predicted 21 returned pairs. Validation on our own seeds: 51 of 51 requests returned 21 pairs; 1,020 replicates gave a mean of 2^-101.0186 (standard error 0.0146 bit), 1.5 standard errors from the preregistered mean; combined with the preregistered sample the 99% bound is 2^-101.0143; 69,190 successes, all genuine semi-free-start collisions. The local emulation of the public-seed request returned 21 pairs (mean of its 20 estimates 2^-100.843).
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo bound under H1: its 99% level relies on the central limit theorem for 32 independent estimates; a heavy right tail would make the sample mean low (conservative) but is not excluded. The organizer replica tests q3 only to within its threshold 2^-101.40 (q3 = 2^-101.40 would give log2 T = 100.71724); the last 0.38 bit rests on the preregistered sample. The replica samples the second-block words from Lemma 2's distribution, so it does not test H1. The `+` reading and the corrected two-bit condition only add conditions. No collision has been observed; the full-scale probability (about 2^-105 per first block) cannot be observed.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 a word-RAM program that evaluates 7 first blocks in 7 x 36-bit lanes of 256-bit words is charged by its counted primitives: 1525 operations per batch of 7 (0.07986 units per first block), with 64 registers and every non-resident constant LOADed at each use.
heuristics.scope: The online term (first-block batches) of the ledger.
heuristics.extrapolation: The count is produced by the shipped program (d1core.calibrate, identical over three groups), with a structural lane-bound check proving that no carry crosses a lane and a liveness check (51 registers). The program is bit-exact against the repository verifier (selftest: 2,100 lanes; development: 21,000 lanes per track; organizer experiment: every lane). The same packing premise was rated plausible in an earlier sha256-r31 filing (H7) and in blake3-r2 filings.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited. Without packed pricing each first block costs one target compression and the claim would be about 103.93.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions and the SFS pair's inner values S (A0..A13, E4..E13, W8..W13 of both members) are used as advice. Their construction is charged at fixed, deliberately generous allowances (upper bounds by scale, not measurements): A_S = 2^74 units for the Step-1 SAT solve (the paper reports 2^38.3 compression-equivalents) and A_C = 2^78 for the characteristic search (cost not published), and all our own computation at DEV = 2^64.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^78.08755); the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: S is verified exactly (every cell, the collision of the published pair under the repository verifier; the organizer experiments' setup asserts every cell). The paper's authors ran both computations with the open-source tool [LLW24a] and published the result, so both are computations an academic group completed; A_S is 2^35 times the reported Step-1 cost, and at 2^21.7 units per CPU-second A_C is about 3 x 10^9 CPU-years and DEV about 2^42 CPU-seconds against about 5,400 CPU-seconds of recorded development (proof.md Section 12).
heuristics.limitations: We did not rerun the paper's SAT solve or characteristic search; the characteristic search has no published cost, so A_C is an allowance, not a measurement. A_C is an upper bound by scale, not a measurement: 2^78 units is about 3 x 10^9 CPU-years at 2^21.7 units per CPU-second, about 140 times the output of a 10^7-core machine (the scale of the largest supercomputers) running for two years, so it bounds any search that an academic group completed and published. The rounded claim is unchanged for A_C up to 2^78 (A_C = 2^79 would give 100.33725); with the earlier allowances 2^56, 2^50, 2^40 the exact log2 T is 100.3372395.
